parts.note: Your tailnet keeps it private, and plain HTTP is fine there. HTTPS (Tailscale Serve) is optional.
parts.title: Pick the address

values.label: Hub address
values.note: Another address: run fleetd init again on the hub and pick it.

guides.test: Reach the hub at its address
guides.title: Where the hub listens
guides.why: Your devices and machines reach the hub at this address; a tailnet keeps it off the internet.

parts.note: The hub's own machine can run agents too: fleetd init on the hub offers it. In the app, Settings › Hub › Machines › Add machine does the same.
parts.title: Add a machine

values.label: On the hub, for a code
On the machine
values.note: Or, from the hub, over SSH: fleetd machine add <ssh host>.

parts.note: A browser and a Linux desktop are on wherever they can run. iOS simulators (a Mac with Xcode) and Android emulators (Linux with KVM) install once a machine is opted in: its switch in Settings › Hub › Machines › Screens.
parts.title: Turn on iOS or Android screens (optional)

guides.title: Machines that run agents
guides.why: Agents run on machines; the hub's own machine can be one.

parts.note: Projects' leads and work nobody started run on it, and so does anyone who picks the hub's API in Settings › Your accounts › Claude. Machines need no login of their own.
parts.title: Give the hub an API key

values.label: Where
values.value: Paste it on Settings › Hub accounts › Claude, with an endpoint if you use a gateway; the app seals it on your device.

parts.note: Without a hub key, leads and work nobody started run on the owner's subscription. Paste the token in Settings › Your accounts › Claude; the app seals it on your device.
parts.title: Or connect your own subscription

parts.note: Each machine's agents run on the Claude account logged in there.
parts.title: Or log Claude in on each machine

guides.test: Read the account's last Test and each machine's login
guides.title: Claude
guides.why: Agents think with Claude: the hub's API key, your subscription, or each machine's login.

parts.note: On Settings › Hub accounts › GitHub: one button, nothing to paste. GitHub hands the App's keys straight to the hub.
parts.title: Create the hub's GitHub App

values.label: Or on the hub, from a terminal

parts.note: Then each person connects their own GitHub in Settings › Your accounts › GitHub, so the PRs of their orders open as them.
parts.title: Install it on the repositories fleetd works on

guides.test: Mint a token for each installation, or ask gh who it is logged in as
guides.title: GitHub
guides.why: The hub opens PRs, reads their CI and merges them.

parts.note: The invite is a link and a code, for one person, good for 7 days. Send it to them yourself.
parts.title: Invite someone

guides.title: Invite people
guides.why: Each person gets their own sign-in, chats and Navi; you choose who is an admin.
